title: lockfile-synth.json — a resolved dependency graph for a tree that ships none
description: Emitted by bin/lockfile-synth.sh. A repo that declares dependencies without pinning them reads exactly like a clean one to every lockfile-driven scanner, so this lane resolves one in a container. The provenance fields are the point: these versions are TODAY's resolution of an unpinned range, not what the project ships, and a consumer that forgets that is publishing findings about a tree nobody has.

skipped.description: Present only when ran is false.

synthesised.description: false covers three different situations — already pinned, nothing to resolve, and resolver failed — which is why reason is required alongside it. Only the first is good news.

exit.description: The resolver's exit code when it failed. Present only on failure; a non-zero exit with no lockfile is an UNRESOLVED tree, which is a coverage void and not a clean result.

lockfile.description: Path relative to the report dir. It MUST end in the ecosystem's canonical filename — osv-scanner selects its extractor by FILE NAME, so package-lock.synth.json is declined outright and scans nothing. The synthetic-ness lives in the directory, never the filename.

sourceUnmodified.description: The scanned tree is byte-unchanged. Asserted rather than assumed because the whole lane would be unacceptable otherwise.

scriptsExecuted.description: npm lane. Resolved with --ignore-scripts, so this is false; a true here would mean third-party install code ran.

buildBackendsExecuted.description: python lane, and it is a PROVENANCE grade rather than a warning. false means the whole graph came from wheel metadata and no third-party build code ran. true means at least one sdist-only dependency had to execute its build backend to state its own requirements, so those versions carry weaker provenance.

from.description: The source manifest the resolution started from.
